lines.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; the zero for refunds of both spouses' 2024 tax on separate 2024 returns is the chosen reading of amb.2025.refund_two_returns (the worksheet tests one 2024 return; the case is zero when neither return itemized with income taxes deducted and refused otherwise, refund.two_itemized_if_two on refund.taxable), and the cap at 2024 line 5d is amb.2025.refund_cap_5d. Exceptions 1 and 5 (i1040gi p. 89, "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025") are refused by refund.not_prior_year on refund.taxable ("Pub. 525, Itemized Deduction Recoveries (Worksheet 2)"), which the line-scoped rendering of line 1 does not show. As the earlier rounds; no wording defect.

Ruling: representation; each amount helper is refund.per_box when its box is answered Yes and zero otherwise, and refund.per_box is $1,550, or $1,950 when the 2024 filing status was single or head of household (label: "The amount for each box checked, $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)"), so the sum is the number of boxes checked times the rate (i1040gi p. 90, line 6). The married-filing-separately condition is in the spouse questions refund.spouse_born and refund.spouse_blind ("If your 2024 filing status was married filing separately, answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent"). As the earlier rounds.
